item.title: Effortful vs. Opportunistic Consumption of Discretionary Time: How Time-Reporting Decisions Influence Extra-Role Effort
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 37.9 ｜ 上线 2026-11-12（1 天前）

Employees often work under incomplete contracts, performing both contracted in-role tasks and valuable but noncontracted extra-role activities. Once employees have completed in-role tasks, discretionary time remains, which they may allocate to extra-role activities or consume opportunistically. This study examines how managers’ time-reporting decisions, as a less intrusive form of control, affect subordinates’ effort-allocation decisions. I propose two opposing predictions. First, managers’ control implementations may signal distrust, resulting in more opportunism and thus less extra-role effort. Second, I identify value signaling as a novel theoretical mechanism through which time-reporting decisions may increase extra-role effort. The main experiment manipulated two factors: the type of time report (aggregated versus disaggregated) and its implementation source (managerial choice versus random assignment) to isolate signaling effects from monitoring effects. Results reveal that when managers choose not to implement disaggregated time reporting—that is, reports that make discretionary time salient—subordinates significantly reduce their extra-role effort. Structural equation modeling shows that value signaling outweighs distrust signaling in driving employees’ effort-allocation decisions. In contrast, when the time-reporting format is randomly assigned, effort remains unchanged, underscoring the signaling role of managerial choice. An additional online experiment shows directionally consistent results with the main experiment. These findings reveal a hidden cost of not controlling and contribute to the literature on incomplete contracts, slack resources, and input-based controls in modern work contexts. This paper was accepted by Ranjani Krishnan, accounting. Funding: This work was supported by the Bijzonder Onderzoeksfonds UGent [Grant BOF/STA/202009/047]. Supplemental Material: The data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.00955 .

item.title: Redeploying the Jockeys: The Intermediary Role of Venture Capital in Entrepreneurial Labor Markets
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 35.4 ｜ 上线 2026-11-12（1 天前）

This paper explores how venture capitalists (VCs) add value by examining their role as labor market intermediaries. Using novel data, I show that VCs create internal labor markets (ILMs) to facilitate entrepreneurial mobility across their portfolio firms. Survey evidence suggests that VCs leverage private information about founders’ abilities to strategically match talent to portfolio firms, creating value for the recipient companies. Consistent with this mechanism of asymmetric learning, I find that (a) former VC partners continue to influence founder mobility, (b) ILM intensity positively predicts VC fund returns, and (c) the ILM effect is stronger when information asymmetry is greater. This paper was accepted by Lin William Cong, finance. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.01626 .

item.title: Deregulation, Market Structure, and the Evolution of U.S. Banking
item.description:

We construct novel network-based measures of U.S. state-level bank deregulation intensity that allow us to separately identify the effects of deregulation on competition and investment opportunities. In contrast to existing studies, we find that increased competition leads to higher deposit funding costs and a reduction in banks’ net interest margins and profitability. In response, banks shift their business models and persistently increase their risk taking. Our findings resolve conflicting evidence in the literature and support theories in which reductions in bank charter values lead to higher bank risk taking. item.title: Improving Energy Price Forecasts: Autometrics With Indicator Saturation
item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 75.4 ｜ 上线 2026-11-11（1 天前）

ABSTRACT In this study, we evaluate Autometrics, an automated model selection method with controls for outliers and location shifts, against artificial neural networks (ANN) and random forests for six monthly energy price series (WTI, Brent, Dubai, US and Russian gas, Australian coal) from IMF data. Autometrics generally delivers lower RMSE/MAPE and higher directional accuracy than the ANN and random forest specifications considered here, particularly in the more volatile oil and coal markets. Autometrics also has the benefit of being interpretable in a familiar regression context as opposed to more “blackbox” machine learning. The CARDt method often delivers predictive accuracy which is not statistically different from Autometrics, but there is some evidence that simple model averaging of the two with intercept‐corrected Autometrics yields further gains relative to either alone.

item.description:
Review of Financial Studies ｜ 综合分 42.0 ｜ 上线 2026-11-10（3 天前） · 在线 2026-11-12

Abstract The quality of investors’ information across different horizons has real effects. When managers care about the effect of investment on their stock price, a decline in the informativeness of investors’ signals about long-term cash flows leads firms with long-term projects to cut investment more than firms with short-term projects. Using a novel, hand-collected measure of project horizons, we confirm this hypothesis: relative to firms with short-term projects, the investment of firms with long-term projects decreases by 3.7% following a 1-standard-deviation drop in the quality of investors’ long-term information. item.title: Labor Market Tightness and the Reversal of Inequality Trends in Germany
item.description:
The Quarterly Journal of Economics ｜ 综合分 35.6 ｜ 上线 2026-11-10（3 天前） · 在线 2026-11-11

Abstract Germany experienced a sharp rise in wage inequality over the two decades leading up to the Great Recession. However, a remarkable trend reversal occurred in 2010—well before the introduction of the minimum wage in 2015—when wages at the bottom of the distribution began to grow more rapidly than those higher up. This paper attributes the reversal to an increasingly tight labor market after the Great Recession, supported by strong domestic demand, and operating through several interrelated and mutually reinforcing channels. Consistent with this hypothesis, job-to-job transition rates and between-job wage growth rose markedly after the recession, especially for workers at the lower rungs of the job ladder. Concurrently, workers increasingly moved from low-paying to higher-paying firms, compressing the worker-weighted distribution of firm wage premia. Tighter labor markets also reduced assortative matching between workers and firms, lowered the skill premium, and weakened firms’ monopsony power.

item.title: Presidential Address: Human Finance: Incorporating Insights from the Life Sciences
item.description:
The Journal of Finance ｜ 综合分 41.0 ｜ 上线 2026-11-10（1 天前） · 在线 2026-11-09

ABSTRACT Many of the key determinants of human behavior identified in the life sciences, such as stress response, impulse control, and mood regulation, remain absent from standard economic and finance models. This paper illustrates how such insights can enhance economic models in the context of inflation expectations. Combining a retrospective survey that elicits personal inflation histories with an experimental intervention that induces the reexperiencing of historic inflation, I show that physiological, emotional, and cognitive stress markers predict heightened inflation expectations and sharper memory recall, while also shaping personal economic narratives. These findings suggest novel policy tools to counter the persistent scars of economic distress and crisis experiences, for example, by designing experiences to provide predictability and control.

item.title: Deadly Disease, Fear, and Ostracism in the Credit Market
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 35.4 ｜ 上线 2026-11-10（1 天前）

This paper exploits the 2014 U.S. Ebola outbreak as a natural experiment to examine how fear distorts mortgage credit allocation. We find a 3.8-percentage-point increase in mortgage denial rates for Black applicants during the outbreak, despite negligible infection risk. Approved Black borrowers have stronger credit profiles and lower default rates, yet are less likely to receive loan modifications when delinquent. These effects are absent in algorithm-driven FinTech lending and reverse quickly postoutbreak—patterns inconsistent with statistical discrimination. Robustness tests rule out alternative explanations related to political cycles, labor market impacts, applicant pool composition changes, and bank financial conditions. Consistent with diagnostic expectation theory, higher exposure to Ebola fear does not result in a significant learning effect during the COVID-19 pandemic. item.title: Uncertainty Attitudes, Subjective Beliefs, and Decisions Under Uncertainty
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 35.4 ｜ 上线 2026-11-10（1 天前）

We conducted survey experiments to gather new data on uncertainty attitudes and subjective beliefs. Our survey targets a general population, focusing on health and financial decisions. We collect data on (i) individual attitudes toward risk and ambiguity, including individual-specific probability weighting and loss aversion, and (ii) individual probabilistic beliefs about events related to the decisions we consider. The joint availability of individual preference parameters and subjective beliefs allows us to study heterogeneity and cross-correlations across these parameters in depth and to estimate structural models of decision making under uncertainty that go beyond subjective expected utility. We find that both preferences and beliefs are highly heterogeneous. Compared with subjective expected utility, prospect theory combined with source-dependent probability weighting fits the data strictly better in some contexts and equally well in others. Prospect theory performs particularly well when the belief distribution is concentrated toward extreme values. item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 32.9 ｜ 上线 2026-11-10（1 天前）

We examine how a profit-driven platform designs its recommender policies under varying privacy protection regimes. We demonstrate a functional equivalence between opt-out protection and unprotected privacy. Notably, granting consumers the autonomy to misrepresent personal data can compel the platform to distort recommendations, inadvertently harming both parties. When recommendations are purely informative, such privacy controls can deter personalization entirely. However, when recommendations also serve an allocative role—controlling product access—algorithmic discrimination may emerge, restricting the disadvantaged minority from valuable opportunities. These findings remain robust even with endogenous profit margins. This paper was accepted by Omar Besbes, revenue management and market analytics. We examine the impact of the war in Ukraine on long-term contracts in energy markets. We find that traded contract volumes fall by 65 percent in the first months of the war. A collapse in bilateral trading contributes most to this decline. To protect themselves from price shocks, firms increasingly turned to long-term contracts already before the war. In sum, our results show that the market continued to serve firms’ hedging needs during the crisis, but bilateral trading networks collapsed, and liquidity was largely provided by centralized markets.

item.title: Channeled Attention and Stable Errors
item.description:
The Quarterly Journal of Economics ｜ 综合分 33.9 ｜ 上线 2026-11-09（2 天前） · 在线 2026-11-10

Abstract People persist in mistaken beliefs even in settings with high stakes, abundant data, and repeated opportunities to learn—settings where standard arguments imply they should correct their errors. We develop an attention-based framework for understanding why errors persist. When a person channels his attention through the lens of his potentially misspecified model, exposure to data is not the same as tracking the statistics necessary to tell him his model is wrong. A model is attentionally stable when the data the person deems relevant will, in the long run, fail to make the model look implausible. Models that erroneously rule things out—e.g., beliefs that a variable doesn’t matter or that a distinction doesn’t exist—tend to be attentionally stable because they divert attention away from data that would refute the models. Conversely, models that erroneously rule things in are less likely to be stable. Whether an error is discovered depends on the structure of the decision problem but is not tightly linked to its level of harm; arbitrarily costly errors can persist while trivially inexpensive ones may be detected. Nevertheless, no error is robust both to changes in the decision environment and to shocks that expand attention: every channeled-attention error is vulnerable to some perturbation that would reveal it. We use the framework to analyze the stability of psychological biases and empirical misconceptions, as well as to explain why fresh eyes catch mistakes, why people use overly coarse rather than overly fine categorizations, and why people recognize errors in others that they miss in themselves.

item.title: Resource‐driven agricultural clusters: Coagglomeration effects of the High Plains Aquifer
item.description:
American Journal of Agricultural Economics ｜ 综合分 43.2 ｜ 上线 2026-11-09（0 天前） · 在线 2026-11-08

Abstract Quantifying the regional economic impacts of crop production is critical for assessing the broader implications of access to natural resources and government policies. However, most existing estimates rely on input–output models with restrictive assumptions, and competing theories of economic mechanisms provide little guidance on the sign or magnitude. We estimate local economic spillovers by exploiting a large increase in crop production that occurred due to the expansion of irrigation in counties overlying the High Plains Aquifer after World War II. While crop production was directly impacted by access to groundwater, we find that livestock product sales also increased significantly, reaching a 235% increase in sales compared to counties outside the aquifer. The primary spillover to non‐farm sectors was an increase in sales in the wholesale sector, perhaps driven by sales of agricultural‐related products. These findings provide evidence of coagglomeration incentives, where clusters of agricultural industries find it optimal to produce within the same region.

item.title: Coherent forecast combination for linearly constrained multiple time series
item.description:
International Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 31.5 ｜ 上线 2026-11-06（6 天前）

Forecasting linearly constrained multiple time series, as those arising in National Accounts, energy systems and supply chain planning, requires that the forecasts of all variables jointly satisfy the underlying accounting or resource-balance identities. When several experts provide forecasts for some or all of the variables, classical forecast combination operates on each variable and ignores the linear constraints, while forecast reconciliation enforces such constraints by using a single forecast per variable. To bridge this gap, we develop an original coherent forecast combination framework, in which the joint problem of combination across experts and coherence across variables is formulated as a linearly constrained optimization problem. Closed-form expressions are derived for the coherent combined forecast and its error covariance matrix, and the statistical properties of the resulting estimators are discussed. A Monte Carlo experiment and a forecasting application to an Australian daily electricity generation dataset confirm that the proposed approach significantly improves forecast accuracy with respect to standard forecast combination and reconciliation alternatives.

item.title: Two-stage least squares with treatment-covariate interactions for treatment effect heterogeneity

Treatment effect heterogeneity with respect to covariates is common in instrumental variable (IV) analyses. We clarify the causal interpretation of the interacted 2sls under the local average treatment effect (LATE) framework when the IV is valid conditional on the covariates. Our main findings are twofold. First, we show that the coefficients on the treatment-covariate interactions from the interacted 2sls identify treatment effect heterogeneity with respect to covariates among compliers for any outcome-generating process if and only if the product of the IV propensity score and the covariates is linear in the covariates, a requirement we call the linear IV-covariate interactions condition. Second, when the covariate vector has dimension K and includes a constant term, we show that the linear IV-covariate interactions condition requires the IV propensity score to take at most K distinct values. The condition holds when (a) the covariates take exactly K distinct values, or (b) the IV is randomly assigned independently of the covariates, but is restrictive beyond these cases. These results underscore the difficulty of interpreting regression coefficients from specifications with treatment-covariate interactions when the covariates are not saturated and the IV is not unconditionally randomized, absent correct specification of the outcome model. We then connect these results to the literature on LATE estimation, and show that under the linear IV-covariate interactions condition, the interacted 2sls with covariates demeaned by their complier means recovers the LATE as a single coefficient.

Abstract In order to quantify the impact of agricultural policy uncertainty on European farmers' investment behavior, we construct a newspaper‐based monthly index of European agricultural policy uncertainty from 2013 to 2023. We use 327,224 newspaper articles to assess and compare the trends in policy uncertainty across five top agricultural producers in Europe, that is, Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Spain and Italy. We connect this index of policy uncertainty to bookkeeping data from 13,706 farms in these five countries over the period 2014–2018 ( N = 68,530) to estimate the relationship between policy uncertainty and investment decisions. In contrast, unanticipated uncertainties, or policy uncertainty shocks, like those caused by the Russian food import ban of 2014 or the US‐China trade war are negatively correlated to farm investment.

item.description:

Abstract Schools across the U.S. have sharply restricted student use of phones during the school day. We evaluate one type of restriction—lockable phone pouches—using nationwide data combining a large-scale teacher survey, GPS pings, standardized test scores, and school administrative records, along with sales records from the largest pouch provider. High schools see modest positive effects, particularly in math, while middle schools see small negative effects. We find little evidence of effects on school attendance and no clear evidence of improvements in self-reported classroom attention or perceived online bullying.

ABSTRACT This study examines the predictability of renewable energy stock returns under economic, financial, and policy uncertainty within a real‐time forecasting framework. item.title: Contest or Contract: Assessing the Effectiveness of Contests in Online Labor Markets
item.description:

Online labor markets have become increasingly popular among companies seeking global access to workers. Some platforms have adopted a contest-based scheme, allowing employers to review multiple submissions before selecting the best one. This practice raises a crucial question: Given a predefined budget, should employers choose a contest or contract scheme for tasks? This study examines the comparative effectiveness of contests versus contracts in achieving better job outcomes, focusing on design tasks characterized by high uncertainty. Using a comprehensive data set from a leading online labor market, we employ multiple empirical strategies, combined with machine learning and text mining techniques, to examine the impact of compensation schemes on job quality. Our results suggest that contract-based jobs yield better performance than contests in the context of ideation tasks. Further analysis, such as examining image similarity among pairwise solutions within a task, identifies “copying” behaviors as a key mechanism undermining the effectiveness of contests. As competition intensity increases, workers have weaker incentives to exert effort, reducing solution quality. Consequently, the negative incentive effects in contests outweigh both the potential positive incentive and parallel effects. Moreover, although information availability can enhance work quality, contests inherently offer limited informational advantages compared with contracts. Taken together, our findings suggest that contract-based schemes are more effective than contests for design tasks, offering important implications for both employers and platform designers in online labor markets. item.description:

A seller wants to sell an item to n buyers. Our analysis reveals three regimes of support information and a new class of robust mechanisms. (ii) When a/b is above another threshold, SPAs are strictly suboptimal, and an optimal mechanism belongs to a class of mechanisms we introduce, which we call pooling auctions (POOL); whenever the highest value is above a threshold, the mechanism still allocates to the highest bidder, but otherwise the mechanism allocates to a uniformly random buyer, that is, pools low types. ABSTRACT Credit scoring requires modeling complex nonlinear relationships between borrower characteristics and default risk, yet highly expressive predictive models often suffer from limited transparency and weak generalization on small‐scale financial datasets.
